title: Explore joint / partner account options
intro: A Dutch gezamenlijke rekening is an everyday account with shared access. Use these soft CTAs to open official sites, then confirm joint eligibility, dual-card fees and exit rules yourself — this block is not a ranking.

items.reason: Onboarding: English-first digital Dutch account many couples use for shared household money. Best for: expats who want app-speed joint or partner setups. Watch-outs: confirm which plan tiers support dual cards, joint access and physical card costs.

Onboarding: Major Dutch retail bank with widely used joint / partner everyday packages. Best for: salary, rent and dual pinpas habits. Watch-outs: compare monthly joint package fees and English support for your branch region.

Onboarding: Full-service Dutch bank with branch depth when both adults need help. Best for: newcomers who want a traditional joint stack. Watch-outs: verify package price, second-card fees and ID/BSN steps on ABN’s site.

Onboarding: Cooperative retail bank with Dutch joint products. Best for: residents who prefer a mainstream gezamenlijke rekening and local presence. Watch-outs: check regional English UX and live tariff PDFs for partner cards.

Onboarding: App-first EU account some households use for shared spending. Best for: digital everyday spend while you settle. Watch-outs: confirm whether a true joint product fits Dutch rent/direct-debit needs before treating it as your only household IBAN.

Onboarding: Spending and FX companion some couples use beside a Dutch joint IBAN. Best for: travel wallets and multi-currency controls. Watch-outs: not a substitute for every Dutch payroll or landlord requirement — verify contracts and joint eligibility.

disclosure: Some links may be affiliate or referral links. If you use them, we may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. Ordering reflects page relevance, not pay-to-rank placement. Always confirm joint fees, dual-card terms and eligibility on the provider’s official pages.
